title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
summary: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears at most twice.
statement: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears at most twice. The relative order of the elements should remain unchanged. After removing the duplicates, the first part of the array nums should contain the final result, and you should return the count of the elements in this part of the array. You must perform this operation in-place without using extra space.
constraints: Modify nums in place so each value occurs at most twice in a sorted prefix. Return its length k; the rest of nums is ignored. Use constant extra space.
hints: A third copy can be detected by looking two positions back in the accepted prefix.
Keep the first two values automatically, then compare each candidate with nums[write-2].
If write<2 or the candidate differs from nums[write-2], write it at nums[write] and advance write.
Compare against the accepted prefix, not a fixed two-position lookback in the original input.
editorial: Maintain a prefix in which every value occurs at most twice. Once two entries have been written, the value two positions behind the write index identifies whether two copies of the candidate are already retained. Sorted order makes this one comparison sufficient. The oracle uses independent occurrence counts capped at two and returns the expected count/prefix pair.

tests.explanation: Return 5 with prefix [1,1,2,2,3], dropping only the third 1.
Return 7 with prefix [0,0,1,1,2,3,3]. Values occurring once are still retained.
